question.prompt: Define the operation “\(\circ\)” by \(x\circ y=4x-3y+xy,\) for all real numbers \(x\) and \(y.\) For how many real numbers \(y\) does \(3\circ y=12?\)

solutions.explanation:
Substituting \(x=3\) makes the product term \(3y\), which cancels the subtracted \(3y\):
\[
3\circ y=4(3)-3y+3y=12.
\]
This equality holds for every real number \(y\), so every real number satisfies the equation. There are infinitely many solutions, hence more than \(4\). The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Substitute and recognize an identity
